olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
Find, as a function of $n$, the sum of the digits of
$$9\times99\times9999\times\cdots\times(10^{2^n}-1),$$
where each factor has twice as many digits as the previous one.

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
For a nonempty set $S$ of integers, let $\sigma(S)$ be the sum of the elements of $S$. Suppose that
$$A=\{a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{11}\}$$
is a set of positive integers with
$$a_1<a_2<\cdots<a_{11},$$
and that, for each positive integer $n\le1500$, there is a subset $S$ of $A$ for which
$$\sigma(S)=n.$$
What is the smallest possible value of $a_{10}$?

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
Chords $AA'$, $BB'$, $CC'$ of a sphere meet at an interior point $P$ but are not contained in a plane. The sphere through $A,B,C,P$ is tangent to the sphere through $A',B',C',P$. Prove that
$$AA'=BB'=CC'.$$

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
Let $P(z)$ be a polynomial with complex coefficients which is of degree $1992$ and has distinct zeros. Prove that there exist complex numbers
$$a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{1992}$$
such that $P(z)$ divides the polynomial
$$\Bigl(\cdots((z-a_1)^2-a_2)^2\cdots-a_{1991}\Bigr)^2-a_{1992}.$$
